{"summary":"Design proposal: Use a normal, resumable onboarding window for installation and GitHub configuration; reserve the menu-bar popover for steady-state monitoring. First run explains the three trust-isolated workspaces, checks Apple Silicon, disk/RAM, network, tools, and permissions, then presents a phased installer for host tools, MSW files, MicroSandbox diagnostics, privileged loopback/hosts setup, base-image creation, workspace creation, and deep verification. Each phase shows progress, expandable logs, its effect, and Retry/Resume/Copy Diagnostics; closing onboarding must not lose state. Privileged work should use an authorized helper, not a hidden sudo shell.

GitHub setup is a first-class wizard: select a workspace, sign in using GitHub’s device flow, display the code with Copy Code and Open GitHub, respect expiry and polling intervals, choose owner and repositories, choose read-only or host-push access, then select a safe verification repository. Before approval, visibly explain that guest access is read-only while the write credential remains in macOS Keychain. Verification maps directly to `msw github setup/verify`: store credentials, bind only guest-read access, clone, create a temporary commit, prove guest push rejection, prove the host-only push path when enabled, delete the branch, and confirm cleanup. Failure must identify the failed stage and whether previous credentials were restored or the workspace was quarantined. The current CLI accepts separate fine-grained PATs, while OAuth device tokens alone cannot preserve its per-workspace read/write boundary; production therefore needs either a GitHub App architecture that preserves separate repository-scoped credentials or a secure noninteractive `msw github setup` contract using pipes/XPC—never tokens in argv, environment, logs, or generic text fields.

After setup, show one calm template status icon with only an attention indicator for actionable degraded, stale, or failed states. Its 380–400 pt keyboard-navigable popover has a fixed header with aggregate health, data age, Refresh, Activity, Settings, and Quit, followed by fixed-order workspace cards for dev, playgrounds, and personal. Each card shows purpose, lifecycle/quarantine state, freshness, compact CPU/memory when running, and the best next action. Visible quick actions are Start when stopped; Open Terminal, Open in Zed, and the most recent site/repository when running; Retry or Diagnostics when unavailable. A labeled workspace-actions menu may contain Stop, Restart, ports, logs, pull, clone, resize, and maintenance, but primary state and recovery must remain visible.

Use a separate resizable detail window with a NavigationSplitView for Overview, Metrics, Logs, Repositories, Ports, GitHub Access, Activity, Backup, and Diagnostics. Stream metrics only while visible; make logs searchable, pausable, bounded, and copyable. Repository rows expose Open in Zed, Open Terminal, Pull, and reviewed Push. Push review must show workspace, repository path, branch, SHA, commits, fast-forward policy, and preserve the CLI’s `PUSH` confirmation; force-with-lease is a distinct higher-risk choice.

Long operations persist in Activity after the popover closes, showing named phases, elapsed time, cancellation when safe, output details, and actionable recovery. Preserve the last good snapshot on communication failure, label it Stale with its observation time, and offer Retry; never translate transport failure into Stopped. Distinguish Mac offline, GitHub unavailable, missing CLI/configuration, stopped VM, quarantine, and partial workspace failure. Monitoring, launch, and popover opening must never start a VM.

Settings contains General (launch at login via SMAppService, polling, appearance), Workspaces (resources and defaults), GitHub (account, repository scope, verify, rotate, remove), Integrations (Ghostty, Zed, favorite ports), Notifications, Diagnostics, Documentation, and About. Store only nonsensitive preferences. Request notification permission only when the user enables a notification category; notify after a baseline only for deduplicated external state changes, threshold breaches, long-operation completion/failure, quarantine, or backup problems, with direct actions back to the affected surface.

Destructive operations use impact-specific sheets rather than generic alerts. Stop/Restart identify interrupted workspace work; `clean --volumes` explicitly warns about unused database volumes; backup shows destination, sensitive contents, and temporary VM stops; restore stays out of the popover, validates checksum/archive, states that managed state is replaced and VMs remain stopped, and requires typed `RESTORE`; GitHub removal explains credential revocation and possible quarantine. Rebuild, recreate, reset-config, deep check, upgrade, update, host repair, and arbitrary `exec` belong in Advanced/Recovery surfaces with explicit scope and progress, not casual quick actions.

For macOS 26, rely on native SwiftUI controls so Liquid Glass appears in system chrome, the popover, toolbars, and navigation. Keep data cards, charts, and logs visually quiet and readable; avoid nested/custom glass decoration. Use SF Symbols, system typography and spacing, semantic colors, system accent, keyboard shortcuts, VoiceOver labels, Dynamic Type, high contrast, Reduce Transparency, and Reduce Motion. Implement with MenuBarExtra window style, Settings and detail WindowGroups, an LSUIElement agent, and an AppKit status-item fallback only if anchoring requires it.

Never hide behind a generic menu: installation progress and blockers; aggregate health and data age; each workspace’s lifecycle, quarantine, and stale state; the primary next action; active-operation progress/cancel/details; GitHub account, repository scope, guest-read versus host-write boundary, and verification result; destructive impact and confirmation; offline recovery; and notification permission rationale. Repository grounding covered `setup.sh` plus `msw status/start/stop/restart`, shell/Zed/open/url/ports/tunnel, clone/repos/pull/push/identity, GitHub setup/status/verify/remove, logs/metrics/disk/resize/clean/check, backup/restore, upgrade/update, exec, and host repair. Recommended integration prerequisite is versioned JSON/JSONL status and progress contracts rather than parsing human CLI output. Verified read-only against README, setup and GitHub guides, `setup.sh`, `bin/msw`, the existing UX artifact, and the official [Apple macOS HIG](https://developer.apple.com/design/human-interface-guidelines/designing-for-macos/) and [GitHub device-flow documentation](https://docs.github.com/en/apps/oauth-apps/building-oauth-apps/authorizing-oauth-apps); no tests, formatters, linters, or mutations were run.","filesChanged":[]}
